title: Improvement of the Accuracy of Lattice Spacing Measurements using NBD Disks Obtained from Precipitates in Ni-Al-Ti Alloy
content: Recently, we have proposed an experimental approach to evaluate local lattice spacing using large diffraction disks. One of the advantages of using diffraction disks instead of diffraction spots is the cost reduction effect, because high-end TEMs are not required for this technique. We first applied this technique to SiGe thin films grown on Si substrates, and we could distinguish Si0.7Ge0.3 from Si even though their d-spacing difference was about 0.002 nm [1, 2]. (Correction: The expression of the d-spacing difference in the body of the reference [2] was wrong, that in the viewgraph was correct.) Then we applied this technique for Ni-Al-Ti alloy and we succeeded in distinguishing the γ matrix and the γ ' precipitate. In this case, their d-spacing difference was also about 0.002 nm [3]. In these papers, we showed how to determine the reciprocal lattice not from the diffraction spots but from the diffraction disks, and we discussed experimental parameters such as convergence angle and camera length to obtain accurate results. In this study, in order to improve the accuracy of this technique, we focused on (1) the machine stability and (2) the human-dependent effect, whether the analyzed results depend on individuals or not. We will write only the essence of the specimen in this paper because we reported it in the previous papers [3, 4]. The Ni-8.5at%Al-5.4at%Ti ingot was prepared by high-frequency induction vacuum furnace. After the solid solution treatment, the specimen was annealed at 940 C for 45 minutes. Thin foil for the TEM observation was prepared by the electrochemical polishing.
